sections.h2: Where are the Tazewell County tax offices in Pekin?
sections.html:
Tazewell County keeps its tax offices together in the McKenzie Building at 11 South Fourth Street in Pekin, ZIP 61554. The Treasurer and Collector is in Suite 308 at 309-477-2284. The Assessment Office and the Board of Review share Suite 410, at 309-477-2275 and 309-477-2277. The treasurer and the board both open at 8 on weekday mornings and close at 4:30.

Each office answers a different question:

  • Treasurer: where to pay, what is owed, tax sale information.
  • Assessment Office: homestead exemption forms, senior freeze renewals, name and address changes, and township assessor contacts.
  • Board of Review: written appeals of an assessed value.

The Assessment Office suggests filing a first homestead exemption in person so staff can check the information. It also notes that its senior freeze mailing reflects a higher income limit of $75,000.

sections.h2: What helps a seller understand Tazewell County?
sections.html:
Pekin, on the Illinois River, is the biggest city in Tazewell County, which belongs to the Peoria metro area. Most residents live along the western edge. Peoria County gave up the land for Tazewell in 1827, and the courthouse then moved from Mackinaw to Pekin, on to Tremont, and back to Pekin in 1849.

The county spans 658 square miles and held 131,343 people in 2020, with an estimate of 130,049 for 2025. Its 58,550 housing units include 7.8 percent sitting vacant. Owners live in about three of every four occupied homes (75.7 percent), and urban areas hold about 78 percent of residents.

School districts shape buyer interest here. Pekin Community High School District 303, Washington District 308 and East Peoria District 309 are the secondary districts, while Morton Community Unit District 709, Eureka Unit District 140 and Tremont District 702 are among the K-12 districts. Peoria's CityLink buses run six routes into the county, and three state fish and wildlife areas (Spring Lake, Powerton Lake and Mackinaw River) lie inside its borders. Pekin's January averages run from a low of 14 degrees to a July high of 86.

sections.h2: What are the Tazewell County installment dates?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's page for the 2026 bill (tax year 2025) names June 1 for the first half and September 1 for the second. It says payments must be received by those dates or interest runs at 1-1/2 percent a month. A bill that arrives late, or never, gives the owner no relief from that interest.

Tazewell County Treasurer dates for the 2026 bill

June 1, 2026First installment due
September 1, 2026Second installment due
October 19, 2026Tax sale of unpaid taxes

The treasurer reports that collections for 2025 exceeded 301 million dollars, which the office disburses to the units of government on each bill. The detailed payment notes are printed on the back of the bill, and written questions to the office are answered by return mail.

sections.h2: What payment methods does Tazewell County accept?
sections.html:
The treasurer takes payments at the counter, by mail and electronically. Checks go to Tazewell County Treasurer, 11 S. Fourth St., Suite 308, Pekin, IL 61554. Electronic payments run by phone at 1-309-925-0025 or online with American Express, MasterCard, Discover, Visa, debit cards, PayPal or e-check.

  • Cards and debit cards add a convenience fee of 2.25 percent of the taxes, never below $1.95 per transaction.
  • E-checks carry a flat $1.25 fee.
  • The provider keeps the fee. None of it goes to Tazewell County.
  • You need the 12-digit parcel number from the top right corner of the bill.

If you cannot find the number, call 309-477-2284 for help. The same fees apply to card payments made at the counter.

sections.h2: How does a Tazewell County owner appeal an assessed value?
sections.html:
Start with the township or county assessor, because a mistake caught early may be fixed without a formal appeal. If that fails, you file a written complaint with the Board of Review. For the 2026 assessment year, the county's posted appeal filing deadline was September 11, 2026, and it has passed. The state rule behind it (35 ILCS 200/16-55) allows 30 calendar days from publication of the assessment list.

Three members make up the Board of Review, named by the County Board, and its session opens on the first Monday of June and ends December 31. It deals only with assessed valuations before equalization, not the tax rate or the bill. The county says a formal appeal needs one of four grounds:

  • The assessor's market value is higher than actual market value, shown by a recent open-market purchase or an appraisal.
  • The assessment is a higher share of market value than the township or county median level in a sales ratio study.
  • The assessment rests on wrong facts, such as a mismeasured lot or building.
  • Similar neighboring properties are assessed lower.

Helpful evidence: the property record card, photos, comparable sales, an appraisal, and Form PTAX-203 from a recent purchase. The county warns that once the bill arrives, it is generally too late to contest that year's assessment. A ruling you dispute can be taken to the state appeals board or to circuit court.

sections.h2: What does the Tazewell County Assessment Office handle besides values?
sections.html:
The office posts forms for several exemptions and relief programs. The list covers Disabled Persons (form 343, with a physician's statement on 343A), Disabled Veterans (342), Returning Veterans (341) and Solar Assessment (330). Annual renewal forms and a Disaster Proclamation form (245) are posted as well.

Owners can also request a name or address change, a split or a combination of parcels. Fraternal and veterans organizations have freeze forms of their own.

The office defines equalization as one uniform percentage raise or cut applied to an area or class of property so that assessments average 33.33 percent of market value. Local assessment officials and the state revenue department both do this work. Township assessors hold the local detail, and the county page links to a directory of them.

sections.h2: What happens if Tazewell County taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
Taxes still unpaid go to registered tax buyers at the yearly sale, set for Monday, October 19 in 2026. The buyer adds interest and penalty, and the treasurer's page carries buyer registration forms and sale results.

The sale transfers a lien. It does not transfer the house. The owner may redeem for 3 years after the sale when the certificate was issued from 2024 forward, with some exceptions such as vacant property. Late-installment interest comes from 35 ILCS 200/21-15, which sets 1 1/2 percent a month or part of a month for a county this size.

The same section puts the interest on a lender that holds enough escrow money and still pays late. Owners who are behind should confirm the payoff and the sale status of the parcel with the treasurer before agreeing to a closing date.

sections.h2: What should a Tazewell County seller do about taxes before closing?
sections.html:
Illinois taxes are paid in arrears, so the bill that comes due in a sale year covers the year before. The purchase contract sets how buyer and seller share it, and the title company carries that out at the table.

  1. Look up the bill with the parcel number and confirm which installments the county shows as paid.
  2. If any installment is late, get the treasurer's payoff figure from Suite 308.
  3. Ask the Assessment Office to remove your homestead or senior exemptions once you no longer live in the house.
  4. Give the title company the correct tax bill address so later bills reach the buyer.

A Tazewell County house needing work can go to a cash buyer as is, with unpaid tax cleared at closing.

faqs.q: Which dates apply to Tazewell County tax payments?
faqs.a: June 1 and September 1, 2026 for the bill covering tax year 2025. Interest of 1-1/2 percent a month follows each date, and the county says a late-arriving bill is no excuse.

faqs.q: Can I pay Tazewell County taxes with a credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. Cards and debit cards are accepted online, by phone at 1-309-925-0025 and at the counter. The provider charges 2.25 percent with a $1.95 minimum, and e-checks cost a flat $1.25.

faqs.q: Did the Tazewell County appeal deadline for 2026 pass?
faqs.a: Yes. The Board of Review posted September 11, 2026 as the filing deadline for the 2026 assessment year, so that window has closed. Future years follow the 30 days after publication rule.

faqs.q: Can the Board of Review change my rate?
faqs.a: No. The board looks only at the assessed valuation before equalization. Rates and totals come from the taxing districts and sit outside an appeal.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about homestead exemptions in Tazewell County?
faqs.a: Ask the Assessment Office at 309-477-2275 in the McKenzie Building, Suite 410. It posts the exemption forms, and it recommends filing a first homestead exemption in person.
